title: Five hard earned lessons about Evals — Ankur Goyal, Braintrust

primary.label: Evaluation, Testing & Benchmarking

domains.rationale: The core domain is LLM evaluation methodology and practice, covering dataset engineering, scoring functions, benchmark comparisons across model providers, and automated eval optimization.

summary: Ankur Goyal, CEO of Braintrust, presents five hard-earned lessons about building effective AI evaluations (evals) at the AI Engineer World's Fair. Lesson 1 argues that effective evals prove their value through three signs: rapid model adoption within 24 hours (citing Notion), a clear path to incorporate user complaints, and offensive use to assess use case viability before shipping. Lesson 2 emphasizes that datasets and scorers must be intentionally engineered—no pre-built dataset perfectly represents real-world usage, and generic off-the-shelf scorers reflect someone else's project specification rather than your own. Lesson 3 introduces context engineering as the evolution of prompt engineering, noting that in modern agentic systems tool definitions and outputs dominate the token budget, and designing tools for LLM consumption (e.g., switching JSON to YAML output) significantly impacts performance. Lesson 4 stresses that new models can transform viability—a feature unviable at ~10% with GPT-4o became viable with Claude 4 Sonnet—and recommends ambitious future-facing evals with model-agnostic proxies. Lesson 5 advocates holistic optimization of the entire system (data, task, scoring) rather than just prompts, introducing Braintrust's Loop feature for automated eval optimization. In Q&A, Goyal addresses overfitting concerns, emphasizing human curation of user feedback over auto-adding, and discusses how ambitious use cases remain non-functional until new model releases enable them.
whyItMatters: These concepts form a coherent framework for AI evaluation engineering that spans the full development lifecycle. The framework begins with treating evals as a core engineering discipline (Lesson 1), which requires custom scoring functions as specifications and dataset reconciliation with production reality (Lesson 2). Context engineering and tool output optimization (Lesson 3) provide the technical foundation for building effective agentic systems, revealing that tools—not system prompts—dominate the token budget and are the primary performance lever. Model-agnostic architecture and ambitious future-facing evals (Lesson 4) ensure teams can capitalize on new model releases that can transform feature viability overnight. System-wide optimization ties everything together (Lesson 5) by demonstrating that optimizing data, task, and scoring holistically produces dramatically better results than prompt-only optimization. The human-in-the-loop feedback curation and overfitting risk concepts ground the framework in real-world practice, ensuring evals stay connected to actual user experience rather than degrading into synthetic benchmarks. Together, these concepts shift the practitioner's mindset from treating evals as a testing afterthought to building a continuous evaluation infrastructure that enables rapid model adoption, proactive viability assessment, and automated system optimization.
temporalContext: The video was published on August 23, 2025, capturing Ankur Goyal's talk at the AI Engineer World's Fair. At the time of recording, Braintrust had raised a $36M Series A (October 2024) and was introducing Loop as a new feature. By the research date of August 21, 2026, Braintrust had raised an $80M Series B (February 2026) at an $800M valuation led by ICONIQ and officially launched Loop with expanded capabilities. The talk references Claude 4 Sonnet (released mid-2025) as enabling a feature that was unviable with GPT-4o, illustrating the rapid pace of model capability improvement during this period. The companion blog post predates the video by one month (July 17, 2025).

concepts.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Scoring
concepts.explanation: Using LLMs to evaluate and score other LLM outputs is a key pattern in automated evaluation pipelines, enabling scalable evaluation of open-ended tasks. The talk emphasizes that even LLM-based scorers must be custom-written to encode domain-specific acceptance criteria.
concepts.importance: Enables automated scoring of subjective or complex outputs that cannot be evaluated with simple rules, though custom scorer design remains critical to avoid adopting someone else's project specification.

concepts.name: Automated Eval Optimization (Braintrust Loop)
concepts.explanation: LLMs can automatically analyze prompts, datasets, and scores to make constructive improvements. Braintrust's Loop feature uses LLMs to optimize the entire eval system, turning unviable features viable.
concepts.importance: Represents a shift from manual eval engineering to AI-assisted optimization, potentially democratizing effective eval practices and enabling continuous system improvement.

concepts.name: Offensive vs Defensive Eval Usage
concepts.explanation: Offensive evals assess use case viability before shipping to determine whether a feature is ready; defensive evals detect regressions in existing features. Both strategies are necessary for a mature eval program.
concepts.importance: Using evals only defensively misses the opportunity to de-risk new features before investment; offensive usage prevents building features that models cannot yet support.

concepts.name: Agent Tool-Calling Architecture (While-Loop Pattern)
concepts.explanation: Modern agent architecture uses a while-loop pattern with iterative tool calls, where the system prompt is a small fraction of total tokens compared to tool definitions and outputs that dominate the token budget.
concepts.importance: Understanding this architecture is prerequisite for context engineering; it explains why tool design matters more than prompt wording for agent performance.

concepts.name: Cross-Model Benchmarking and Viability Thresholds
concepts.explanation: Benchmarking features across model providers reveals viability thresholds: GPT-4o scored ~10% (unviable), Gemini 2.5 Pro scored 1%, while Claude 4 Sonnet made the same feature viable. This demonstrates model capability is often the gating factor for feature viability.
concepts.importance: Cross-model benchmarking identifies which models enable specific use cases and prevents architectural lock-in that would block adoption of capability improvements.

concepts.name: Overfitting Risk in Eval Datasets
concepts.explanation: Overfitting to datasets without user feedback is a greater risk than overfitting with user feedback. Datasets disconnected from real usage create false confidence in model performance.
concepts.importance: Prevents teams from optimizing against metrics that do not reflect real-world performance, which is the primary failure mode of eval programs.

concepts.name: Token Distribution Analysis in Agents
concepts.explanation: Analysis of agent traces shows tools very significantly dominate the token budget, with system prompts being a small fraction of total tokens in agentic systems.
concepts.importance: Provides quantitative evidence that tool design, not prompt engineering, is the primary lever for optimizing agent systems.

concepts.name: Ambitious Future-Facing Evals
concepts.explanation: Creating evals that test capabilities beyond current model performance allows teams to detect when new model releases cross viability thresholds, enabling rapid feature launches within weeks of a model release.
concepts.importance: Without ambitious evals, teams miss the opportunity to ship features immediately when new models make them viable, losing first-mover advantage.

concepts.name: Meta-Optimization (LLM Self-Improvement)
concepts.explanation: Braintrust used Loop to optimize Loop's own prompts, demonstrating that LLMs can improve their own tooling through automated eval optimization. This was confirmed via the official blog post 'Evals are a team sport: How we built Loop' published November 2025.
concepts.importance: Validates the concept of automated eval optimization by showing it works even on the optimization tool itself, suggesting broad applicability of the approach.

concepts.name: Model Release as Feature Enabler
concepts.explanation: New model releases can make previously unviable features viable overnight. A feature sat at GPT-4o-level performance (~10%) for a long time before becoming viable with Claude 4 Sonnet, enabling a product launch two weeks after the model's release.
concepts.importance: Teams must maintain ambitious evals and model-agnostic architectures to capitalize on capability jumps from new model releases, which can transform feature viability.

concepts.name: Evals as Engineering Discipline
concepts.explanation: The talk frames evaluations as a core engineering discipline requiring intentional design, continuous investment, and organizational integration rather than an afterthought or optional tooling.
concepts.importance: Foundational principle that all other lessons build upon; shifts evals from testing overhead to development enabler that proves its value through rapid model adoption and user feedback incorporation.

concepts.name: Custom Scoring Functions as Specifications
concepts.explanation: Custom-written scorers function as specs or PRDs for the AI application, encoding domain-specific acceptance criteria rather than generic quality metrics. Using off-the-shelf scorers means adopting someone else's project specification.
concepts.importance: Misaligned scorers evaluate against the wrong criteria, creating false confidence in model performance and missing real failure modes specific to the application.

concepts.name: Dataset Reconciliation with Production Reality
concepts.explanation: No pre-built dataset perfectly represents real-world usage; datasets must be continuously reconciled with actual production data and user behavior to remain representative.
concepts.importance: Stale or synthetic datasets create a false sense of model performance and miss real failure modes that users encounter in production.

concepts.name: Context Engineering
concepts.explanation: Context engineering supersedes prompt engineering in agentic systems. Most tokens come from tool definitions and their outputs, not the system prompt. The entire context window must be engineered for LLM consumption.
concepts.importance: Optimizing only the system prompt leaves the majority of token budget unoptimized; tool design is the primary lever for agent performance improvement.

concepts.name: Tool Definition and Output Optimization
concepts.explanation: Tools should be designed for what the LLM needs to see, not as reflections of existing APIs. Output format choices such as switching from JSON to YAML significantly impact LLM performance due to token efficiency.
concepts.importance: Tool design is the highest-leverage optimization in agentic systems since tools dominate the token budget and directly determine what information the LLM can effectively process.

concepts.name: Model-Agnostic Architecture
concepts.explanation: Systems should use model-agnostic proxies and architectures that enable rapid model swapping across providers, allowing teams to benchmark and adopt new models within 24 hours of release.
concepts.importance: New models can transform feature viability overnight; architectural lock-in to a single provider prevents rapid adoption of capability improvements and creates competitive disadvantage.

concepts.name: System-Wide Optimization (Data + Task + Scoring)
concepts.explanation: Optimization should target the entire evaluation system including datasets, task (prompt/agentic system/tools), and scoring functions rather than prompts alone. Full-system optimization produces dramatic performance improvements that prompt-only optimization cannot achieve.
concepts.importance: Prompt-only optimization leaves significant performance gains unrealized; holistic optimization can turn unviable features viable by improving all components simultaneously.

concepts.name: Human-in-the-Loop Feedback Curation
concepts.explanation: Human judgment with taste is essential for curating user feedback into eval datasets. Auto-adding all user feedback risks introducing noise and degrading dataset quality rather than improving it.
concepts.importance: Prevents dataset degradation from noisy feedback while maintaining a connection to real-world usage patterns that keeps evals grounded in production reality.

concepts.name: Rapid Model Adoption Workflow
concepts.explanation: Effective eval infrastructure enables shipping product updates with new models within 24 hours of release, as demonstrated by Notion's workflow. This requires evals that serve as deployment gates and rapid benchmarking pipelines.
concepts.importance: Time-to-market for new model capabilities is a competitive advantage; eval infrastructure quality is the gating factor that determines how quickly teams can leverage new models.

concepts.name: Token Efficiency in Agent Systems
concepts.explanation: Token efficiency in tool definitions and outputs directly impacts LLM task performance. Format choices like YAML over JSON reduce token consumption and improve results in agentic systems where tools dominate the token budget.
concepts.importance: Token efficiency is a measurable engineering optimization that directly correlates with agent performance in production and can be systematically improved through format and structure choices.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Brief introduction to the talk about lessons learned over time in AI product development and evals.

sections.title: Lesson 1: Effective Evals Speak for Themselves
sections.summary: Three signs that evals are providing value: (1) ability to launch product updates with new models within 24 hours, citing Notion's example; (2) a clear path to incorporate user complaints into evals; (3) using evals offensively to understand use case viability before shipping, rather than just regression testing.

sections.title: Lesson 2: Great Evals Need to Be Intentionally Engineered
sections.summary: Datasets and scorers must be engineered, not taken off-the-shelf. No dataset perfectly represents reality; datasets need continuous reconciliation with real-world usage. Scorers should be custom-written like specs or PRDs for the AI application. Using generic scorers means adopting someone else's project specification.

sections.title: Lesson 3: Context Engineering is the New Prompt Engineering
sections.summary: Modern agent prompts include system prompts plus iterative tool calls in a loop. Most tokens come from tool definitions and outputs, not the system prompt. Tools should be designed for LLM consumption rather than as reflections of existing APIs. Example: switching tool output from JSON to YAML improved performance due to token efficiency.

sections.title: Lesson 4: Be Prepared for a New Model to Change Everything
sections.summary: New models can make previously unviable features viable. Benchmark showed a feature going from ~10% (unviable) with GPT-4o to viable with Claude 4 Sonnet, enabling launch two weeks after model release. Recommends ambitious future-facing evals and model-agnostic proxies for rapid testing across providers.

sections.title: Lesson 5: Optimize the Entire Evaluation System, Not Just the Prompts
sections.summary: Advocates holistic optimization of the entire AI system: data for evals, task (prompt/agentic system/tools), and scoring functions. Benchmark comparing prompt-only optimization vs full-system optimization showed dramatic differences, turning unviable features viable. Introduces Braintrust's 'loop' feature that auto-optimizes prompts, datasets, and scores using LLMs, supporting multiple models including Claude 4 Sonnet/Opus, o3, o4 mini, Gemini, and custom fine-tuned models.

sections.title: Recap of the Five Lessons
sections.summary: Summarizes all five lessons: evals should speak for themselves and demonstrate competence; engineer the entire system (not just prompts, avoid only synthetic/HuggingFace datasets and off-the-shelf scores); think carefully about context and design tools like prompts; be ready for new models to change everything and potentially require ripping out existing architecture; optimize the whole system including data, task, and scoring functions.

sections.title: Q&A: Overfitting, Token Distribution, and Model Changes
sections.summary: Audience Q&A covers three topics. (1) Overfitting: Goyal is more worried about overfitting to datasets without user feedback than with it; Braintrust deliberately requires human curation of user feedback rather than auto-adding it to datasets. (2) Token distribution: analysis of agent traces shows tools very significantly dominate the token budget, reinforcing the importance of tool definition and output design. (3) Model changes: the loop feature benchmark sat at GPT-4o-level performance for a long time before becoming viable with newer models; some simple use cases like movie quote classification have worked since GPT-3.5, while ambitious ones remain non-functional until new model releases. A government use case illustrates the need to distinguish 'answer is correct but user doesn't like it' from incorrect answers.

organization.name: Braintrust
organization.summary: Braintrust is an AI evaluation and observability platform founded in August 2023 by Ankur Goyal in San Francisco, California. The platform provides evaluation datasets, custom scorers (LLM-as-a-judge, code, and human), experiment management, CI/CD deployment gating, production tracing, and automated optimization through its Loop feature. Braintrust's customers include Notion, Stripe, Zapier, Vercel, Ramp, Replit, Cloudflare, Dropbox, Box, OpenAI, Navan, BILL, and HubSpot. As of February 2026, the company raised an $80M Series B at an $800M post-money valuation led by ICONIQ Capital, with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, Greylock, Elad Gil, and basecase capital. The talk presents five lessons about building effective AI evaluations based on Braintrust's production experience with hundreds of customers.
organization.status: Active, private company. Series B funded ($80M, Feb 2026, $800M valuation led by ICONIQ). CEO: Ankur Goyal. Headquartered in San Francisco, CA. Approximately 151 employees.

technologies.label: AI Evaluation Infrastructure
technologies.summary: The talk centers on AI evaluation as a core engineering discipline. Effective evals require custom scoring functions that serve as specifications for the AI application, continuously reconciled datasets grounded in production reality, and the ability to use evals offensively to assess use case viability before shipping. The talk identifies three signs that evals provide value: rapid model adoption within 24 hours, a clear path to incorporate user complaints, and offensive use for viability assessment. Braintrust's Evaluate product provides the platform capabilities for this including datasets, scorers, experiments, deployment gating, and production-to-eval feedback loops.
technologies.role: Central technology discussed throughout all five lessons and the Q&A session, forming the backbone of the entire presentation.

technologies.label: Context Engineering
technologies.summary: Context engineering supersedes prompt engineering in modern agentic systems. The talk demonstrates that in agent architectures using iterative tool calls, tools very significantly dominate the token budget, making tool design the primary performance lever rather than system prompt wording. A concrete example shows switching tool output from JSON to YAML significantly improved LLM performance due to token efficiency. This is a technique rather than a specific product.
technologies.role: Primary focus of Lesson 3 and reinforced in Q&A with quantitative token distribution analysis showing tools dominate the token budget.

technologies.label: Model-Agnostic Proxy Architecture
technologies.summary: Model-agnostic proxy architecture enables rapid model swapping across providers, allowing teams to benchmark and adopt new models within 24 hours of release. The talk demonstrates how new models (Claude 4 Sonnet) can transform feature viability overnight from unviable (~10% with GPT-4o) to viable, making architectural flexibility and model-agnostic design critical for competitive advantage. Braintrust Gateway implements this as a proxy for model calls.
technologies.role: Supporting technology in Lesson 4 about new models changing everything, enabling the rapid model adoption and cross-model benchmarking described throughout the talk.

technologies.label: Automated Eval Optimization
technologies.summary: Automated eval optimization uses LLMs to analyze and improve prompts, datasets, and scoring functions holistically rather than focusing on prompts alone. Braintrust's Loop feature implements this as an AI assistant with access to production traces, datasets, scorers, and experiment results. The talk demonstrates that full-system optimization produces dramatically better results than prompt-only optimization, and meta-optimization has been validated where Loop optimized its own prompts.
technologies.role: Primary focus of Lesson 5, demonstrated with Braintrust Loop feature showing automated optimization of the entire eval system (prompts, datasets, scores).
